newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 2.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Ingwe Coal Corporation has reinforced its dominance of the global steam coal market by buying an Australian coal company in a deal worth 800 million rand - a move which could boost its exports 80 percent by 2005.
- Randgold & Exploration Co Ltd was preparing to list five of its mines on the Nasdeq screen-based trading system in the U.S. from Wednesday, industry analysts said on Tuesday.
- South Africa has been in the driver's seat in negotiations with the World Bank for its first loan, which could even be denominated in rands if the country gets its way.
- The finance ministry has sent a questionnaire to banks in a bid to find market makers over the Reserve Bank's role in placing state debt.

- Government's investment incentive scheme came into effect on Tuesday after the measures were bulldozed through from announcement to implementation in an attempt to fulfil a key element of the strategy for growth, emploment and redistribution on time.

- DLJ Pleiade Investment, the investment house controlled by New Africa Investments Limited (Nail), is putting the final touches to a private equity fund to raise 500 million rand from local institutional investors, sources close to the company said on Tuesday.

- Ingwe Coal Corporation, the coal mining company in the Gencor Ltd fold, has reinforced its position as the world's largest exporter of steam coal by buying a 96.3 percent stake in Coal Mines of Australia (CMAL) from the Australian Mutual Provident Society for 310 million rand.
- The state has been investigating ways to reduce its exposure to risk in the bond market by asking private firms if theyr are willing to make a market in government bonds.

- Alan Munro, the executive director of Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd said on Tuesday that he was under pressure from shareholders to close the Leeundoorn gold mine, which was not at all economically viable.
- Unidentified investors on Tuesday snapped up four percent of equity of Consolidated Frame Textiles' and a sizeable chunk of Frame Group Holdings' shares.

- The Truth and Reconciliation Commission is poised to swoop on suspected human rights violators countrywide following a decision to swop the "velvet glove" approach for a "fist of steel," TRC chairman Archbishop Desmond Tutu has disclosed.

- The Inkatha Freedom Party re-entered the constitution-making process yesterday and gave notice that it would push for constitutional protection for Zulu King Goodwill Zwelithini and KwaZulu Natal traditional leaders.

- Finance Minister Trevor Manuel and delegates attending the International Monetary Fund and World bank annual general meeting will embark on an extensive roadshow across the U.S. to promote South Africa as a destination for investors, leading government officials said on Tuesday.
